## Map Xfield / Yfield

```{r}

plot_bota <- function(df, taxa_rank){
  # Take :  
  # - a botanical dataframe, 
  # - a rank of taxa for coloration
  # Do :
  # - Create plot
  # Return :
  # - the plot of stems
  
  # Create plot
  p <- ggplot(data = df, aes(x = Xfield, y = Yfield)) +
    geom_point(
      aes(color = data[[taxa_rank]], size = CircCorr),
      shape = 21,       # Cercle (21–25 permettent un remplissage)
      fill = NA,        # Creux (pas de remplissage)
      stroke = 1        # Épaisseur du contour
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
  
  # Return the plot
  p
}
```

```{r}

select_tax <- function(Data, Level, Name){
  # Take : 
  # - Data : the dataframe with contain Taxas
  # - Level : The name of the column to filter
  # - Name : The value to filter the column
  # Do :
  # - Select the focus in Data
  # Return :
  # - focus : the Data filtered
  
  # Select the focus in Data
  focus <- Data[Data[Level] == Name,]
  
  # Return
  focus
}
```

### Density grid

```{r}

# 4 functions :
# - normalization
# - make_density_grid
# - plot_grid
# - plot_hist

normalization <- function(count) {
  # Take : 
  # - count column
  # Do :
  # - Normalisation of count
  # Return :
  # - density column
  
  # Normalisation
  density <-  count / sum(count)
  
  # Return
  density
}

make_density_grid <- function(bota_focus, R){
  # Take : 
  # - bota_focus dataframe (Xfield, Yfield)
  # - R the radius of count around the pixel position
  # Do :
  # - Create the doublet (x,y)
  # - Add indices (i,j)
  # - Add the density to the doublet
  # Return :
  # - The density grid in a triplet (x, y, density)
  
  # Create the doublet (x,y)
  grid <- expand.grid(
    x = seq(10,300,10), # X position of samples
    y = seq(10,400,10) # Y position of samples
    )
  # Add indices
  grid$i <- grid$x / 10
  grid$j <- grid$y / 10
  
  # Add the density to the doublet (x,y)
  grid$density <- pmap_int( # Apply a function to each coordinates (x,y)
  list(grid$x, grid$y), # Element of iterations
  \(x, y) sum((x - bota_focus$Xfield)^2 + # Count TRUE ...
              (y - bota_focus$Yfield)^2 <= R^2, # ... on Pytagore condition (dx²-dy² <= R²)
              na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>% normalization() # Convert count to density
  
  # Return
  grid
}

plot_grid <- function(grid, col_name){
  # Take :
  # - grid : the triplet (x,y,z)
  # - col_name : the name of column for color
  # Do:
  # - Create the ggplot
  # Return :
  # - plot
  
  # Create the ggplot
  p <- ggplot(grid, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = .data[[col_name]])) + # use col_name to take the column
    coord_fixed() +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(fill = "Densité")
  
  # Return ggplot
  p
}

plot_hist <- function(grid,col_name){
  # Take :
  # - grid : the triplet (x,y,z)
  # - col_name : the name of column for color
  # Do:
  # - Create the ggplot
  # Return :
  # - plot
  
  # Create the ggplot histogram
  p <- ggplot(grid, aes(x = .data[[col_name]])) +
    geom_histogram() +
    theme_minimal()
  
  # Return ggplot
  p
}
```

## Filtre Gaussien

```{r}

# 2 functions of convertion :
# - col_to_img
# - img_to_col

col_to_img <- function(z){
  # Take :
  # - z : the z of the grid (x,y,z)
  # Do:
  # - Convert (z) in matrix of size (ni,nj)
  # - Convert matrix in image of size (ni,nj)
  # Return :
  # - image of imager package
  
  # Convert (z) in matrix of size (ni,nj)
  mat <- matrix(z, nrow = 30, ncol = 40, byrow = FALSE)
  
  # Convert matrix in image of size (ni,nj)
  img <- as.cimg(mat, x=30, y=40)
  
  # Return
  img
}

img_to_col <- function(img){
  # Take :
  # - img : image of imager package
  # Do:
  # - Create the doublet (x,y)
  # - Put image value in column (z)
  # Return :
  # - grid triplet (x,y,z)
  
  # Create the doublet (x,y)
  grid <- expand.grid(
    x = seq(10,300,10),
    y = seq(10,400,10)
    )
  # Put image value in column (z)
  grid$z <- as.vector(img)
  
  # Return cols
  grid
}
```

# Cluster

## MCMC (Metropolis Hasting) sur image smooth

```{r}

mcmc_sampling <- function(img,n_iter){
  # Take :
  # - img : image to sample
  # - 
  # Do :
  # - Set seed
  # - Convert img to matrix
  # - Get size of the matrix
  # - Get real x and y
  # - Set initial points (indices)
  # - Initalise samples storage
  # - MCMC loop to fill samples
  # Return:
  # - samples : postions of samples (x,y)
  
  # Set seed
  set.seed(123)
  
  # Convert img to matrix
  z <- as.matrix(img)
  
  # Get size of the matrix
  nx <- nrow(z)
  ny <- ncol(z)
  
  # Get real x and y
  x_vals <- seq(10, 10*(nx-1), length.out = nx)  # exemple correspondance i -> x
  y_vals <- seq(10, 10*(ny-1), length.out = ny)  # exemple correspondance j -> y
  
  # Set initial points (indices)
  i <- sample(1:nx, 1)
  j <- sample(1:ny, 1)
  
  # Initalise samples storage
  samples <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_iter, ncol = 2)
  
  # MCMC loop to fill samples
  for(k in 1:n_iter){
    
    # propose new point (continu)
    i_new <- i + runif(1, -1, 1)  # déplacement continu
    j_new <- j + runif(1, -1, 1)
    
    # stay inside bounds
    i_new <- max(min(i_new, nx), 1)
    j_new <- max(min(j_new, ny), 1)
    
    # interpolation bilinéaire pour obtenir z continu
    i0 <- floor(i_new); i1 <- ceiling(i_new)
    j0 <- floor(j_new); j1 <- ceiling(j_new)
    di <- i_new - i0
    dj <- j_new - j0
    
    # handle edges
    i1 <- min(i1, nx)
    j1 <- min(j1, ny)
    
    # bilinear interpolation
    z_new <- (1-di)*(1-dj)*z[i0,j0] + di*(1-dj)*z[i0,j1] +
             (1-di)*dj*z[i1,j0] + di*dj*z[i1,j1]
    
    z_current <- z[i,j]
    
    # accept/reject
    alpha <- z_new / z_current
    if(runif(1) < alpha){
      i <- i_new
      j <- j_new
    }
    
    # stocker en coordonnées réelles
    samples[k, ] <- c(
      x_vals[1] + (i-1)*(x_vals[2]-x_vals[1]),
      y_vals[1] + (j-1)*(y_vals[2]-y_vals[1])
    )
  }
  
  # Rename columns
  samples <- as.data.frame(samples) %>%
    rename("x"="V1","y"="V2")
  
  # Return
  samples
}
```

## K_means

```{r}

kmeans_clustering <- function(k, samples){
  # Take :
  # - k : number of clusters to create
  # - samples : samples position (x,y)
  # Do:
  # - Set seed
  # - Apply K-means function
  # - Add labels to dataframe
  # Return :
  # - df_kmeans : triplet dataframe (x, y, cluster)
  
  # Set seed
  set.seed(123)
  
  # Apply K-means function
  kmeans_result <- kmeans(samples, centers = k, nstart = 25)  # nstart = nombre d'initialisations
  
  # Add labels to dataframe
  df_kmeans <- data.frame(
    x = samples[,1],
    y = samples[,2],
    cluster = factor(kmeans_result$cluster)
  )
  
  # Return
  df_kmeans
}

# df_kmeans <- kmeans_clustering(20, mcmc_samples)

```

## Double plot (MCMC and Clustering)

```{r}

# Apply MCMC function
mcmc_samples <- mcmc_sampling(img_smooth)
# Get MCMC plot
p1 <- ggplot(mcmc_samples, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, color = "red", size = 0.5) +
  coord_fixed() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "MCMC") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 400),
    breaks = seq(0, 400, by = 100))

# Apply clustering function
df_kmeans <- kmeans_clustering(20, mcmc_samples)
# Get clustering plot
p2 <- ggplot(df_kmeans, aes(x = x, y = y, color = cluster)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 0.5) +
  stat_density_2d(aes(fill = cluster, group = cluster),
                  color = "black", alpha = 0.1, geom = "polygon") +
  coord_fixed() +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")+
  labs(title = "K-means clustering") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 400, by = 100)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 400),
    breaks = seq(0, 400, by = 100))

# Plot MCMC and Clustering
grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol = 2)
```

**Problème:**

On ne peux pas différencier par arbre, mais par cluster. Un même cluster peux contenir 1 gros arbre ou plusieurs petits. On fait l'hypothèse que la taille du cluster est proportionnelle à la Basal Area des arbres qui le compose.

## Analyse Intertype

```{r}

# 1. Créer un objet ppp pour les deux types
xrange <- range(c(grid_BAG$i, grid_DIC$i))
yrange <- range(c(grid_BAG$j, grid_DIC$j))
window <- owin(xrange, yrange)

# Créer les points avec marquage
pp <- ppp(
  x = c(grid_BAG$i, grid_DIC$i),
  y = c(grid_BAG$j, grid_DIC$j),
  window = window,
  marks = factor(c(rep("type1", nrow(grid_BAG)),
                   rep("type2", nrow(grid_DIC))))
)

# 2. Calculer la fonction K-cross
Kc <- Kcross(pp, "type1", "type2")

# 3. Calculer la L-cross
Lc <- Lcross(pp, "type1", "type2")

# 4. Display
plot(Lc, main = "Analyse intertype Attraction/Répulsion")

```

## Confidence interval

```{r}
envelope_result <- envelope(
  pp,
  fun = Lcross,
  i = "type1",
  j = "type2",
  nsim = 99,       # nombre de simulations
  rank = 1,        # enveloppe 95%
  global = TRUE    # enveloppe globale
)

plot(envelope_result,
     main = "Analyse intertype avec enveloppes Monte Carlo",
     legendargs = list(x = "topleft", legend = c("Lcross", "Enveloppe 95% Monte Carlo")))

```

***Bagassa guianensis*** **et *Dicorynia guianensis* sont naturellement attirés**

## Data Importation

```{r}


import_genet <- function(){
  # Set directory
  setwd(PROJECT_PATH)
  
  # GH marker
  diet_data_GH <- read_obifasta("metabar_PP_GH.simple.clean.c10.l40.taxo.ann.fasta")
  diet_data_GH %<>% extract_features("obitag_bestmatch","obitag_bestid","obitag_rank","scientific_name",'taxid')
  
  # 18S marker
  diet_data_18S <- read_obifasta("metabar_PP_18s.simple.clean.c10.l80.taxo.ann.fasta")
  diet_data_18S %<>% extract_features("obitag_bestmatch","obitag_bestid","obitag_rank","scientific_name",'taxid')
  
  # ITS marker
  diet_data_ITS <- read_obifasta("metabar_PP_ITS.simple.clean.c10.l180.taxo.ann.fasta")
  diet_data_ITS %<>% extract_features("obitag_bestmatch","obitag_bestid","obitag_rank","scientific_name",'taxid')
  
  # Centralize data in Named List (no duplication, just ref)
  diet_data_list <- setNames(
    list(diet_data_GH, # df
         diet_data_18S, 
         diet_data_ITS), 
    c("GH","18S","ITS") # names
  )
}

extract_feature <- function(data,key){
  # Extract key (obiclean_weight, or other)
  # with ROBIFastread function
  # given the dataframe
  diet_mat <- extract_readcount(data, key=key)
  # The result is a dgCMatrix
  diet_mat
}
```

## taxid \> Famille/Genre/Espèce

```{r}


# Function Take the rank name for a give rank
get_rank <- function(x, rank) {
  val <- x$name[x$rank == rank]
  if(length(val) == 0) NA else val
}

# Fonction to create taxid ref for local genet data from ncbi
create_taxid_ref <- function(){
  # Take all unique taxid from clean genet data
  all_unique_taxid <- c(diet_data_GH$taxid, 
                      diet_data_18S$taxid, 
                      diet_data_ITS$taxid) %>% unique()
  
  # from unique taxid import list of full path
  taxo <- classification(all_unique_taxid, "ncbi")

  # Import F, G, s from taxo thanks to get.rank()
  tax_table <- map_dfr(taxo, ~tibble(
    family  = get_rank(.x, "family"),
    genus   = get_rank(.x, "genus"),
    species = get_rank(.x, "species")
  ))
  
  # remove the genus from the specie
  tax_table$species <- word(tax_table$species, 2) # keep the second word
  
  # Add taxid to FGs
  tax_table$taxid <- all_unique_taxid
}

get_FGs <-function(data){
  # Get Familly, Genus, species from faxid reference
  data <- left_join(data, tax_table, by="taxid")
  data
}

```

## Correspondance Bota/Génèt

```{r}

# Ref pcr / (x,y)
create_sample_ref <- function(){
  # Import physical data of samples
  data_samples <- read.table(
    "/home/jean/Bureau/doi_10_5061_dryad_dc28m__v20181029/Zinger_et_al_metabar_PP1_samples.txt",
    header = TRUE,
    comment.char = "#"
  )
  # Select and split pcr
  sample_ref <- data_samples %>%
    select(pcr,x,y) %>%
    separate(pcr, into = c("sample_loc", "sample_rep"), sep = "_") %>%
    distinct(sample_loc, x, y)
  
  # Return Ref
  sample_ref
}

# Add x and y data genet
Add_x_y_from_pcr <- function(samples_count){
  data <- left_join(samples_count, pcr_ref ,by="sample_loc")
  data
}

mean_by_pcrLoc <- function(data){
  data <- left_join(data ,pcr_ref ,by="pcr_loc")
}

```

```{r}
# Create env (only the first time)

# Bota Model

bota_focus <- select_tax(bota, Level, Name)
## Density grid

p1 <- plot_grid(grid,"density") +

## Get Familly, Gender, species cols

## Select taxa
genet_focus <- select_tax(genet, level, Name) %>%
  filter(!is.na(.data[[level]])) # col family, genus or specie
## sample_name / count (for the targetted taxa)
### Matrix
sample_matrix <- extract_feature(genet_focus,"obiclean_weight") %>%
  rowSums() # sum on diet_id
### Dataframe
sample_df <- sample_matrix %>% 
  as.data.frame() 
### give colnames
sample_df$sample_id <- rownames(sample_df)
sample_df$count <- sample_df$.
sample_df <- sample_df %>%
  select(sample_id,count)
### mean by sample_loc
sample_df <- sample_df %>%
  separate(sample_id, into = c("sample_loc", "sample_rep"), sep = "_") %>%
  group_by(sample_loc) %>%
  summarise("count" = mean(count))
### Add (x,y)
sample_df <- left_join(sample_df, sample_ref, by="sample_loc")
### Normalisation
sample_df$density <- normalization(sample_df$count)

# Plot
p3 <- plot_grid(sample_df,"density")+
  labs(title = "eDNA density")

# Compare results
## df join
df_compare <- sample_df %>%
  rename(dens_genet = density) %>% # rename density
  left_join(grid, by = c("x", "y")) %>% # left join
  rename(dens_bota = density) %>% # rename density
  select(-count) %>%
  mutate(err_abs = dens_genet - dens_bota) %>%
  mutate(err_rel = (dens_genet - dens_bota) / dens_bota)

# Create the plot
p4 <- ggplot(df_compare, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = err_abs)) + # use col_name to take the column
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "lightpink",      # valeurs négatives
    mid = "white",    # neutre (0)
    high = "lightgreen", # valeurs positives
    midpoint = 0
  ) +
  coord_fixed() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(fill = "Density") +
  labs(title = "Absolute error")

# Results
grid.arrange(p1, p3, p4, ncol = 3)

# Diagnostic : Justesse et précision
hist(df_compare$dens_diff)

```
